## `glmGamPoi2` fork

The `glmGamPoi2` package is a fork of the [existing glmGamPoi package](https://github.com/const-ae/glmGamPoi) which aims to optimize performance and memory use.
Multiple "knobs" are provided which can be used to enable the various implementations provided.

Primarily, the `glm_gp` entrypoint now has an added `perf_optim` parameter, which can be used to enable/disable specific optimizations at will.

## Currently supported parameters

We demonstrate below the various parameters currently introduced via the `perf_optim` parameter.
First, we load the library, initialize a synthetic dataset, and generate a reference object:

```{r}
library(glmGamPoi2)

counts <- matrix(rnbinom(256, mu = 4, size = 0.25), 32, 8)
fit_ref <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = FALSE)
```

### `offset_as_vec`

The `offset_as_vec` parameter allows representing the per-gene/per-observation offsets as a vector when they are not configured to vary across any one observation:

```{r}
head(fit_ref[["Offset"]]) # we can see this is a matrix

fit_vec <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(offset_as_vec = TRUE))
head(fit_vec[["Offset"]]) # we can see this is now a vector
```

### `delay_mu`

The `delay_mu` parameter allows representing the prediction matrix `Mu` via a [thunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunk) interface instead of eagerly computing a dense representation:

```{r}
head(fit_ref[["Mu"]]) # we can see this is a matrix

fit_delayed <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(delay_mu = TRUE))

is.function(fit_delayed[["Mu"]]) # we can see this is now a _function_

# demonstration of the thunk'd Mu API
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](), fit_ref[["Mu"]])
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](i = 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][1, , drop = FALSE])
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](j = 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][, 1, drop = FALSE])
all.equal(fit_delayed[["Mu"]](1L, 1L), fit_ref[["Mu"]][1, 1, drop = FALSE])
```

### `use_nr_overdisp_impl` and `do_parallel`

The `use_nr_overdisp_impl` and `do_parallel` flags do not change output shape, but modify behaviour of internal routines:

- `use_nr_overdisp_impl`: enables the use of an alternative overdispersion estimation routine written in `C++`
- `do_parallel`: enables parallelization of various steps across the package

Please note that while testing/benchmarking has found that these do not _significantly_ affect result outputs, there are edge cases (especially for ill-conditioned fits with high deviance on the resulting fit) where enabling `use_nr_overdisp_impl` can lead to slightly different results.

```{r}
fit_alt <- glm_gp(counts, perf_optim = list(do_parallel = 2L, use_nr_overdisp_impl = TRUE))

# we can see these have no effect on resulting model parameters
all.equal(fit_alt[["overdispersions"]], fit_ref[["overdispersions"]])
all.equal(fit_alt[["Beta"]], fit_ref[["Beta"]])
```

## Changing package-wide defaults

Finally, to improve usability when one wishes to change parameters package wide, the `set_perf_optim_opts` helper is provided.
Notably, it has a `v2` parameter, which allows for a coarse-grain toggle of all recommended optimizations:

```{r}
set_perf_optim_opts(v2 = TRUE)

get_perf_optim_opts()

fit_v2 <- glm_gp(counts)

# we can see that all optimizations have now been enabled
head(fit_v2[["Offset"]])
is.function(fit_v2[["Mu"]])
```
